headline: The Gold Rewards Card's 0.025% bonus is described both as a card bonus (outranked by the EcoCard) and as a separate relationship bonus that stacks, so the correct credit could be $140 or $142.

issues.summary: Gold expects 6.85% (5.5 base + 0.75 Green boost + 0.6 EcoCard), which treats the Gold Rewards Card 0.025% purely as a credit-card bonus outranked by the EcoCard. doc_013 instead calls it a relationship bonus "on top of the base rate", and doc_045 says relationship bonuses stack with card bonuses, which gives 6.875% and a $142.00 credit.
evidence: doc_savings_accounts_gold_account_013: "As a Gold Rewards Card holder, you receive an additional 0.025% relationship bonus APY on top of the base rate." and the example "Total APY with the bonus: 6.0%" (5.5 + 0.025 is 5.525)

doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_045: "credit card APY bonuses DO stack with other types of bonuses, such as: ... Relationship bonuses for holding multiple Rho-Bank products"; its example lists "Gold Rewards Card: +0.025% APY bonus" among non-stacking card bonuses
db credit_card_accounts: cc_wl94k7m3p8_gold "Gold Rewards Card" ACTIVE, cc_wl94k7m3p8_eco "EcoCard", cc_wl94k7m3p8_platinum
replay: credit 142.0 -> verified match False (accounts, bank_account_transaction_history differ)
issues.why_it_matters: Both readings are supported by required documents. An agent that applies doc_013 literally credits $142.00 and fails the DB check.
issues.suggested_fix: State in doc_013 that the 0.025% is the Gold Rewards Card credit-card APY bonus (subject to highest-only stacking), and fix its "Total APY ... 6.0%" example.

solution_check: Base 5.5% (gold_001/002); Green+Gold pairing gives +0.75% (green_checking_001); highest card bonus EcoCard +0.6% (gold_014, stacking per doc_045). Expected 6.85%. Actual = 408 x 12 / 96000 = 5.10%. Credit = $140.00, matching gold[6], unless the doc_013 relationship bonus is added on top.
prior_note: Same doc_013/014 ambiguity as before; raised from Minor to Major so it matches the identical defect in task_095, since a reasonable agent can stack the bonus and change the credit amount.
notes: submit_interest_discrepancy_report_7294 calls add_to_db("interest_discrepancy_reports", ...), but TransactionalDB has no such table, so add_to_db returns False and the tool still prints success. The report persists nothing; only its tool name in agent_discoverable_tools (a write, always logged) is graded. Its expected_apy, actual_apy, and amount_difference arguments therefore never affect the DB result; only the apply_savings_account_credit_6831 amount does (it changes accounts.current_holdings and a transaction_id hashed from the amount). The savings docs say interest is "compounded daily" from a daily periodic rate, but every posted credit equals balance x APY / 12 exactly. Gold uses that monthly convention, and an agent that back-solves actual_apy from the posted credit adopts it naturally. A literal daily-compounding computation would give a slightly different credit. Only the credit amount is graded, so expected_apy 6.85 vs 6.875 in the report cannot fail the task on its own.
